about: Synthetic security news for the E2E journeys (tests/e2e/seed.py). Invented outlets, an invented CVE, documentation addresses (RFC 5737) and .example domains only. APT28 is the actor in the checked-in reference fixture tests/entities/fixtures/ref. e2e-art-1 also has a stored technique (T1566.001, which the ATT&CK reference fixture already lists for APT28: an article reporting a catalogue link), and e2e-art-4 carries a stored extraction result (what the local model returned for it), so the story page shows techniques of all three kinds offline: one the article names by id, likely ones and a possible one.

articles.title: APT28 exploits ExampleGate zero-day CVE-2026-1111
articles.dek: A state-backed group is breaking into ExampleGate VPN appliances through an unpatched flaw.
paragraphs: Example Research Lab has seen APT28 exploit CVE-2026-1111, a critical flaw in ExampleGate VPN appliances, against small offices and home labs since early November.
The lab says the first break-ins began with spearphishing emails that carried a booby-trapped attachment.
The attackers used the server 203.0.113.7 for command and control and the domain evil-c2[.]example to stage their tools.
After the first break-in the group, also known as Fancy Bear, planted a web shell on each appliance and copied its configuration, including saved passwords.
ExampleGate owners should install the vendor's fixed release today, check their logs for any contact with 203.0.113.7, and change every password the appliance stored.
The lab shared its detection notes with the vendor, which confirmed the flaw and published an advisory for CVE-2026-1111.
Night Desk users can compare their own connection logs with the addresses named in this report from the story page.

articles.title: More ExampleGate break-ins tied to APT28
articles.dek: A second team confirms the campaign against ExampleGate appliances.
paragraphs: Northwind Security also saw APT28 exploit CVE-2026-1111 in ExampleGate VPN appliances, with traffic to 203.0.113.7 from every device it examined.
Its responders found the same web shell and the same staging domain, evil-c2[.]example, on appliances in three countries.
The team says the campaign is still running and that unpatched ExampleGate appliances are being found and broken into within hours.
Northwind recommends blocking 203.0.113.7 at the firewall while the fixed release is rolled out, and reviewing which accounts logged in to each appliance this month.

articles.title: Router maker ships long-awaited firmware for older home models
articles.dek: An update for routers that stopped getting fixes two years ago.
paragraphs: A router maker has shipped new firmware for home models it stopped updating two years ago, after owners asked for fixes to the web admin page.
The release closes several bugs in the admin page and turns on automatic updates by default.
Owners can install it from the admin page or let the router fetch it overnight.
The company says it will keep shipping security fixes for these models until the end of next year.

articles.title: ExampleRAT phishing wave hits small accounting firms
articles.dek: Booby-trapped invoices open the door to a remote-access trojan.
paragraphs: Harbor Threat Notes tracked a new ExampleRAT phishing wave against small accounting firms during November.
The emails carried a booby-trapped invoice document, the delivery method MITRE ATT&CK lists as T1566.001.
Once opened, ExampleRAT dropped a small web shell on the firm's internet-facing mail server so the operators could come back later.
The operators then searched shared folders for spreadsheets and text files that held saved passwords.
ExampleRAT talks to its operators over ordinary web traffic, which makes it hard to spot in firewall logs.
Firms should block macro-enabled invoices from outside senders and review which files on shared drives hold passwords.
